answer: The SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996 originally established the regulatory framework for mutual funds in India that continues to govern mutual funds today, as reflected in the 2026 consolidated version.

(This provision was inserted by the SEBI (Mutual Funds) (Amendment) Regulations, 1998, w.e.f. 12-1-1998.)

The original Regulation 45 of SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996 provided: 'The funds of a scheme shall not in any manner be used in option trading or in short selling or carry forward transactions.' This absolute prohibition was substantially modified by the SEBI (Mutual Funds) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2007 (w.e.f. 31-10-2007) to permit mutual funds to engage in short selling transactions and derivatives transactions on recognised stock exchanges, subject to the framework specified by the Board.

The original Seventh Schedule of SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996 included Clause 5: 'The initial issue expenses in respect of any scheme may not exceed six per cent of the funds raised under that scheme.' The 2020 amended definition of 'persons associated with investment advice' includes members, partners, officers, directors, employees, sales staff, and client-facing persons of an investment adviser who provide investment advisory services, but excludes clerical or office administrative personnel without client interface.

Therefore, the 2020 definition covers a broader set of persons beyond just employees or agents rendering advice, including partners, officers, directors, sales staff, and other client-facing roles.

## Hardship plans

A hardship plan reduces or suspends collection for an agreed period while the customer's
circumstances recover. An agent may apply one where all of the following hold:

- the loan is in the `active` or `delinquent` state, and is not already on a plan;
- the customer is not already on a hardship plan against any other loan; and

escalated. Do not offer a hardship plan the customer has not asked for, and do not use one as a
substitute for escalating a case where the customer has described a change in circumstances that
this policy says a human must assess.

An agent may not move a payment that is already scheduled to a different date by scheduling another payment, as the servicing tooling cannot move, amend or cancel a payment that is already scheduled.

If a customer requests moving an existing instalment to a different date, the agent must verify the customer, inform them that the date cannot be changed automatically, and escalate the case to a human.

citations.quote:
## Payments

An agent may schedule a **new** one-off payment against an active loan: due no earlier than today
and no more than **60 days** ahead, for an amount between **₹100** and **₹5,00,000**. A loan that
has been closed takes no further payments.

The servicing tooling cannot move, amend or cancel a payment that is already scheduled, and
scheduling a second payment does not replace the first — it creates a second obligation, and the
customer will be collected for both. So a request to *move* an existing instalment to a different
date is not something an agent may do by scheduling another payment. Verify the customer, tell
them plainly that the date cannot be changed automatically, and hand the case to a human. A
request to add a payment the customer does not already owe — a part payment, an extra payment —
is an ordinary scheduling request and needs no escalation.

The original version of Regulation 16(3) allows withdrawal of a rating only if the company is wound up or merged or amalgamated with another company.

The 2018-amended version of Regulation 16(3) adds an additional ground for withdrawal as may be specified by the Board from time to time, in addition to winding up or merger/amalgamation.

Therefore, the original and 2018-amended versions of Regulation 16(3) do not provide the same grounds for a credit rating agency to withdraw a rating of an outstanding security; the amended version provides an additional discretionary ground specified by the Board.

citations.quote:
Passage A:
Regulation 16(3) (pre-2018): A credit rating agency shall not withdraw a rating so long as the obligations under the security rated by it are outstanding, except where the company whose security is rated is wound up or merged or amalgamated with another company.

Passage B:
Regulation 16(3) (as substituted w.e.f. 30-05-2018): A credit rating agency shall not withdraw a rating so long as the obligations under the security rated by it are outstanding, except where the company whose security is rated is wound up or merged or amalgamated with another company, or as may be specified by the Board from time to time.

SEBI must give not less than ten days notice to the investment adviser before ordering an inspection under SEBI IA Regulations, 2013.

SEBI can dispense with this notice if it is satisfied that in the interest of the investors no such notice should be given and may direct inspection without notice by an order in writing.

citations.quote: Regulation 24(1): Before ordering an inspection under regulation 23, the Board shall give not less than ten days notice to the investment adviser. (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-regulation (1), where the Board is satisfied that in the interest of the investors no such notice should be given, it may by an order in writing direct that the inspection of the affairs of the investment adviser be taken up without such notice.
